title: Merchant onboarding credit planner (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: back-of-envelope for a merchant-focused onboarding credit that balances activation lift vs cost. This is a working scratchpad — rough numbers, lots of assumptions.

Context / constraints:
- Target: reduce time-to-first-value (TFV) for merchants integrating embeddings + chat flows.
- Want 2-4 pilot customers to reach LTV>commit within 90 days.
- Budget: practical early program budget ~ $30k total credits across cohort.

Key assumptions (placeholders):
- Hosted token cost (internal blended): $0.0006 / 1k tokens (internal infra + model avg). <-- internal unit cost, NOT public price.
- Avg merchant pilot throughput: 20k tokens / day during active onboarding (typical indexing + testing + prod spikes).
- Active onboarding window: 21 days (3 weeks).
- Expected retention to paying plan after credits expire: 25% (conservative).
- ARPA if convert (monthly): $1,500 (small-mid merchant) -> 12-month ARR ~ $18k.
- CAC target for this channel: <= $3k (incl. SRE/SE time).

Simple credit sizing examples:
1) Flat 3-week usage credit to cover onboarding bursts:
   - Daily tokens: 20k tokens/day * 21 days = 420k tokens total.
   - Cost to Redwood: 420k / 1k * $0.0006 = $0.252 (this feels wrong; check units)
   - Correcting: if internal unit cost is $0.0006 per 1 token? No — make units clear: assume $0.60 per 1M tokens (i.e., $0.0000006 per token) — that leads to tiny numbers.
   - Re-anchor: set internal cost = $0.60 per 1k tokens (i.e., $0.0006/token). That was intended earlier but easily confusing. New canonical: $0.60 per 1k tokens = $0.0006/token.
   - With $0.60 / 1k tokens -> 420k tokens = 420 * $0.60 = $252 cost to us.
   - So a 3-week cover for 20k/day -> ~$250 per merchant in raw token spend.

2) Heavier pilot (100k tokens/day):
   - 100k * 21 = 2.1M tokens -> 2100 * $0.60 = $1,260 cost.

Heuristics to pick credit size:
- Small pilot (low-touch): give a coupon covering up to 500k tokens (~$300) + 1-hour SE office hours.
- Medium pilot (SE-assisted): cover up to 2M tokens (~$1.2k) + 4 hours SE + onboarding docs + a quick eval.
- Full integration (white glove): 5M tokens (~$3k) + up to 12 hours SE + early access to dedicated capacity trial.

Break-even check (per merchant):
- If conversion rate = 25% and ARR on convert = $18k, expected ARR per offered merchant = 0.25 * $18k = $4.5k.
- If we allocate $1.5k credits + ~$1k SE cost (amortized) => $2.5k upfront cost. Expected payback: 4.5k ARR vs 2.5k cost => OK over 12 months (CAC < 50% of ARR acceptable for this motion).

Session / retention levers:
- Tie credits to success milestones (index X docs, reach N queries) to avoid one-time burst usage then disappear.
- Use staged credits: 50% upfront, 50% on milestone completion (e.g., embed index run + API calls >= 50k).
- Limit credits to specific endpoints (embeddings, search rerank) to prevent abuse via bulk generative runs.

Burst protection & anti-abuse:
- Per-merchant daily cap when on promo: e.g., 200k tokens/day unless approved.
- Require valid baseline metric: verified integration via sample query + simple smoke-test script.

Alternate packaging: prepaid retainer + token top-ups
- Offer small retainer $500/month that includes 1M tokens + discounted overage. Helps convert pilots to recurring.
- Example: Retainer gives 1M tokens ($600 cost to us) but billed at $1,200 to merchant = $600 gross margin in month 1. Need to factor SE time churn.

Cohort budget simulation (n=20 merchants):
- If we give median credit $1k each -> total credit spend = $20k.
- Expected converts = 25% -> 5 converts -> ARR uplift ~ 5 * $18k = $90k. Payback in < 12 months likely.

Edge calculations / sensitivity table (quick mental):
- If conversion = 15% instead of 25% -> expected ARR = 3 * 18k = $54k; spend $20k -> still OK but longer payback.
- If average pilot burns 4M tokens (cost $2.4k) -> spend for 20 merchants = $48k -> need higher convert rate or larger ARPA.

UX considerations (practical):
- Single use promo codes per merchant (tie to org id) to avoid sharing.
- Clear dashboard showing remaining promo token balance and milestone progress.
- Auto-reminder ~3 days before promo exhaustion with suggestions to convert to retainer.

Operational items / TODOs:
- [ ] Validate internal blended token cost with infra finance (CF: unit = $ per 1k tokens).
- [ ] Add SE time hourly rates and estimate per-pilot SE effort buckets.
- [ ] Draft promo code naming conventions + lifecycle (expiry, revocation rules).
- [ ] Mockup merchant dashboard copy for "promo credits" + CTAs.
- [ ] Create a small internal playbook for step-up offers at day 7 and day 14.

Questions / open tradeoffs:
- Should credits be refundable or convertible to account credit? (Affects accounting).
- Do we gate credits behind a minimal integration test (makes fraud protection easier but adds friction)?
- What's an acceptable per-merchant SE time budget? How do we amortize SE salary into CAC?

Short examples to keep for comms:
- "Starter Onramp": 500k tokens (~$300 cost) + 1h SE -> goal: self-serve SMB merchants.
- "Scale Pilot": 2M tokens (~$1.2k cost) + 4h SE -> goal: PLG -> paid conversion.
- "Enterprise Trial": 5M tokens (~$3k cost) + dedicated onboarding -> goal: validate SLA/Private deployment interest.

Closing notes:
- Token spend alone looks cheap relative to SE costs and potential ARR. The lever that matters most is conversion rate and ARPA.
- Favor staged credits and milestone gating to reduce waste.
- Next: run 10-person pilot with mixed credit sizes (A/B test small vs medium) and track conversion/week-8.

Last edit notes: kept raw math visible so product + finance can quickly iterate. Update after finance confirms internal cost-per-1k-token and SE cost model.
